title: Area of Regular Polygons
contentObjective: I can find the area of a regular polygon by decomposing it into triangles.
languageObjective: I can explain my steps using the words regular polygon, decompose, triangle, and composite.

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: The Rooftop Garden
revealWordProblem.text: The firm is designing a regular decagon-shaped rooftop garden bed. It decomposes into 10 congruent triangles from the center, each with a base of 3 feet and a height of 4 feet. The garden center charges $5 per square foot for soil and plants. What is the total cost to fill the garden bed?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: One triangle: A = ½ × 3 × 4 = 6 sq ft. The decagon has 10 sides, so it has 10 triangles: 10 × 6 = 60 sq ft. Cost = 60 × $5 = $300.

conceptIntro.heading: How do we find the area of a regular polygon?
conceptIntro.intro: A regular polygon has all sides and all angles equal. We can decompose it (break it apart) into equal triangles from the center, then add up their areas.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: A regular polygon splits into the same number of triangles as it has sides, so total area = (one triangle's area) × (number of sides).

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: My hexagon has 6 equal sides. Each side is 6 feet, and each center triangle has a height of 5.2 feet.
First I find one triangle: A = ½ × base × height = ½ × 6 × 5.2.
I multiply: 6 × 5.2 = 31.2, then ½ × 31.2 = 15.6 square feet.
A hexagon has 6 sides, so it has 6 equal triangles.
I multiply: 6 × 15.6 = 93.6. So the total area is 93.6 square feet.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Now a smaller regular pentagon: each of its 5 triangles has base 4 cm and height 3 cm.
First find one triangle: ½ × 4 × 3. What is 4 × 3? Yes, 12, and half of 12 is 6 sq cm.
A pentagon has 5 sides, so how many triangles? Yes, 5.
Multiply: 5 × 6 = 30, so the total area is 30 square centimeters.

onLevel.labelEs: Une cada polígono con su área total.
hintsEs: Cada tarjeta de polígono muestra su número de triángulos y el planteamiento ½ × b × h de un triángulo; la pareja es el área TOTAL.
Trabaja en dos pasos: evalúa la parte ½ × b × h y luego multiplica por el número de triángulos indicado.
Tarjeta del hexágono: halla ½ × 6 × 5.2 para un triángulo y luego multiplica por 6 para obtener el total que buscas.

onLevel.instructions: Calculate the total area of each regular polygon, then sort from smallest to largest area.
onLevel.hint: Draw lines to split the figure into rectangles or triangles.
hints: Each card shows the polygon's total area at the end — compare that number to 90 sq ft.
'Area ≥ 90' includes exactly 90; anything below 90 goes in the other group.
First card: the pentagon's total is 110 sq ft. Is 110 at least 90? Place it, then compare each remaining card.
onLevel.explanation: Each card ends with the polygon's total area, so sorting is a comparison to 90 sq ft. The pentagon (110 sq ft) and the hexagon (93.6 sq ft) are at least 90, while the octagon (76.8 sq ft) and the square (40 sq ft) fall below 90 — more sides does not automatically mean more area, since the triangle sizes differ.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada tarjeta termina con el área total del polígono, así que clasificar es comparar con 90 pies cuadrados. El pentágono (110) y el hexágono (93.6) llegan a 90 o más, mientras que el octágono (76.8) y el cuadrado (40) quedan por debajo de 90: tener más lados no significa automáticamente más área, porque los triángulos tienen tamaños distintos.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Calcula el área total de cada polígono regular y después ordénalos del área más pequeña a la más grande.
hintsEs: Cada tarjeta muestra el área total del polígono al final: compara ese número con 90 pies².
'Área ≥ 90' incluye exactamente 90; cualquier cosa por debajo de 90 va en el otro grupo.
Primera tarjeta: el total del pentágono es 110 pies². ¿Es 110 al menos 90? Colócala y compara cada tarjeta restante.

onLevel.instructions: A regular hexagon has 6 triangles, each with base 5 ft. The total area is 75 sq ft. What is the height of each triangle? (Hint: 75 = 6 × ½ × 5 × h → 75 = 15h → h = 5)
onLevel.label: Find the triangle height: total area = 75 sq ft, 6 triangles, base = 5 ft
onLevel.hint: Composite figure = made of two or more simple shapes.
hints: The 75 sq ft is the WHOLE hexagon — six equal triangles share it.
Since 6 × ½ × 5 = 15, every foot of height adds 15 sq ft. So the equation is 75 = 15 × h.
Divide 75 by 15 and place your point at that height.
onLevel.explanation: All six triangles share the 75 sq ft, and each one is ½ × 5 × h, so the total is 6 × ½ × 5 × h = 15h. Solving 75 = 15h gives h = 5, so the point belongs at 5 on the number line.
onLevel.explanationEs: Los seis triángulos comparten los 75 pies cuadrados, y cada uno es ½ × 5 × h, así que el total es 6 × ½ × 5 × h = 15h. Al resolver 75 = 15h se obtiene h = 5, así que el punto va en el 5 de la recta numérica.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Find the area of one triangle

onLevel.correctWork: The student forgot to multiply by ½ when finding the triangle's area. A = ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 sq ft, so Total = 5 × 12 = 60 sq ft.
hints: Look at Step 3. What is the formula for the area of a triangle?
A triangle's area is ½ × base × height, not just base × height. One triangle = ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 sq ft, so the total is 5 × 12 = 60 sq ft.
onLevel.explanation: In the step that finds one triangle's area, the student used 6 × 4 = 24 and left out the ½. A triangle is half of the rectangle with the same base and height, so A = ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 sq ft and the pentagon's total is 5 × 12 = 60 sq ft.
onLevel.explanationEs: En el paso que halla el área de un triángulo, el estudiante usó 6 × 4 = 24 y dejó fuera el ½. Un triángulo es la mitad del rectángulo con la misma base y altura, así que A = ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 pies cuadrados y el total del pentágono es 5 × 12 = 60 pies cuadrados.

extending.title: Find the Area Error
extending.correctWork: To find total area, multiply (not add): Total = 10.75 × 6 = 64.5 sq m. Six equal triangles means 6 times one triangle's area.
hints: Look at Step 4. What operation should you use to combine 6 equal triangles?
The student added 10.75 + 6 instead of multiplying 10.75 × 6.
extending.explanation: One triangle at 10.75 sq m is correct, but the last step added the 6 instead of using it as a count. Six congruent triangles means six copies of that area, so Total = 10.75 × 6 = 64.5 sq m.
extending.explanationEs: Un triángulo de 10.75 metros cuadrados está bien, pero el último paso sumó el 6 en lugar de usarlo como cantidad. Seis triángulos congruentes significan seis copias de esa área, así que el total es 10.75 × 6 = 64.5 metros cuadrados.

extending.prompt: A regular hexagon and a regular pentagon both have triangles with the same base (6 ft) and the same height (5 ft). Which polygon has the greater total area? Explain why the number of sides matters.
extending.sentenceFrame: One triangle's area is ½ × ___ × ___ = ___. The hexagon has ___ triangles so its area is ___. The pentagon has ___ triangles so its area is ___. The ___ has more area because ___.
extending.hint: Identify each shape; write area formula; add results.
hints: Both polygons use identical triangles (base 6 ft, height 5 ft) — only the NUMBER of triangles differs.
Find one triangle's area with ½ × 6 × 5, then multiply by 6 for the hexagon and by 5 for the pentagon.
Compute ½ × 6 × 5 for one triangle. Then compare 6 copies with 5 copies and explain why the counts matter.
extending.explanation: One triangle is ½ × 6 × 5 = 15 sq ft in both polygons, so the only difference is how many copies each shape holds: the hexagon has 6 for 90 sq ft and the pentagon has 5 for 75 sq ft. The hexagon has the greater area because the number of sides is exactly the number of identical triangles you get to add.
extending.explanationEs: Un triángulo mide ½ × 6 × 5 = 15 pies cuadrados en los dos polígonos, así que la única diferencia es cuántas copias tiene cada figura: el hexágono tiene 6 para 90 pies cuadrados y el pentágono tiene 5 para 75. El hexágono tiene mayor área porque el número de lados es exactamente la cantidad de triángulos iguales que puedes sumar.
extending.promptEs: Un hexágono regular y un pentágono regular tienen triángulos con la misma base (6 pies) y la misma altura (5 pies). ¿Cuál polígono tiene mayor área total? Explica por qué importa la cantidad de lados.
hintsEs: Ambos polígonos usan triángulos idénticos (base 6 pies, altura 5 pies): solo cambia el NÚMERO de triángulos.
Halla el área de un triángulo con ½ × 6 × 5 y luego multiplica por 6 para el hexágono y por 5 para el pentágono.
Calcula ½ × 6 × 5 para un triángulo. Luego compara 6 copias con 5 copias y explica por qué importa la cantidad.

extending.instructions: Plot the vertices of a regular hexagon centered at (6, 5) with vertices at approximately (6,8), (8.6,6.5), (8.6,3.5), (6,2), (3.4,3.5), (3.4,6.5). Notice how the hexagon can be split into 6 triangles from the center.
extending.label: Plot the hexagon vertices and visualize the 6 triangles from the center.
extending.hint: Plot vertices to see which simple shapes form the composite.
hints: The six targets A–F are the hexagon's corners; the center of the shape is at (6, 5).
Plot carefully — x-values like 8.6 land between gridlines 8 and 9. Then imagine spokes from (6, 5) to each corner.
Start with A at (6, 8) and go around in order to F. Drawing the spokes reveals the 6 triangles the formula counts.
extending.explanation: Plotting A (6, 8) through F (3.4, 6.5) in order outlines a regular hexagon whose center is (6, 5). Drawing a spoke from that center to each of the six vertices cuts the hexagon into the 6 congruent triangles the area formula counts, which is why every vertex has to be placed accurately — including the 8.6 and 3.4 values that land between gridlines.
extending.explanationEs: Marcar A (6, 8) hasta F (3.4, 6.5) en orden dibuja un hexágono regular cuyo centro es (6, 5). Trazar un radio desde ese centro hasta cada uno de los seis vértices corta el hexágono en los 6 triángulos congruentes que cuenta la fórmula del área, y por eso cada vértice debe ubicarse con precisión, incluidos los valores 8.6 y 3.4 que caen entre las líneas de la cuadrícula.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Area of Regular Polygons is stopping after finding the area of ONE triangle and reporting that as the total area — or adding the number of triangles instead of multiplying. Remember: total area = (one triangle's area) × (number of sides), not (one triangle's area) + (number of sides).

exitTicket.stem: A regular pentagon is decomposed into 5 triangles from its center. Each triangle has a base of 7 inches and a height of 4.8 inches. What is the total area of the pentagon?
exitTicket.explanation: One triangle: A = 1/2 x 7 x 4.8 = 16.8 sq in. Total = 5 x 16.8 = 84 square inches.
choiceFeedback: That's one triangle — multiply by all 5 triangles.
You skipped the ½ — each triangle is ½ × 7 × 4.8.
Right value, wrong unit — area is square inches.
hints: Two steps hide in this problem: one triangle's area first, then all 5 triangles together.
One triangle is ½ × 7 × 4.8; the pentagon is 5 of those. Skipping either step leads to a wrong path.
Take half of 7 × 4.8 to get one triangle's area, then multiply that by the 5 triangles.

questions.stem: Why do we divide by 2 when finding the area of a triangle?
choices: A triangle is exactly half of a rectangle with the same base and height
The base is always twice the height
We always divide area formulas by 2
questions.explanation: A triangle with base b and height h fits inside a rectangle with the same base and height. The triangle covers exactly half the rectangle, so A = ½ × b × h.

questions.stem: A triangle has an area of 24 sq ft and a base of 8 ft. What is the height?
What is the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm?
questions.explanation: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 square centimeters.
